newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Hebron deal needed for better relations.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Hebron deal needed for better relations.

text.p: Egypt welcomed on Tuesday reports of progress in Israeli-Palestinian talks and said its troubled relationship with Israel would improve as soon as these talks ended in agreement on the West Bank town of Hebron.

A deal would create a new atmosphere and reassure Syria about Israel's intentions, President Hosni Mubarak told reporters after talks in the Red Sea resort of Hurghada with Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.
Mordechai told a joint news conference that Israel would continue peace talks with the Palestinians on all pending issues after the deal on the long-delayed redeployment in Hebron.
"If today we sign the agreement about Hebron, we can continue with all the redeployment and we can have some answers about other problems that are now on the table," he said.
"I believe that we are very close to signing a Hebron agreement and immediately afterwards we will continue in all the issues on the agenda between us and the Palestinians," he added.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat met on the border of Gaza and Israel on Tuesday but failed to clinch the Hebron agreement.
U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross said they made real progress and negotiating teams would meet on Wednesday.

Mubarak, a vociferous critic of Netanyahu's policies towards Middle East peace, said he was encouraged by what he heard from Netanyahu in a phone conversation on Monday evening and at his meeting with the Israeli defence minister.
On at least two occasions in the past three months Mubarak, whose country signed a peace treaty with Israel in 1979, has refused to meet Netanyahu until Hebron is settled.
"I was happy yesterday when Mr Netanyahu told me they had achieved great progress...I had good impressions from the prime minister," he said.

But pressed on whether progress alone was enough to restore Israeli-Egyptian relations, Mubarak said: "Relations between states go through phases and sometimes the atmosphere is an obstacle to cooperation.
"I believe that as soon as they reach an agreement (on Hebron)...then this will lead to a big upturn in clearing the air and to more cooperation and interaction."
"That's why I was pleased to see the minister tell me we are about to get there. I hope this is for real...This would give confidence to the peace process," Mubarak added.

"Solving the Hebron problem and starting the final status negotiations could...create trust with Syria, for it to start negotiations. Syria has some demands in the negotiations and hope this atmosphere will help both sides," he said.
Mordechai also brought up the effect on the Syrian track of Middle East negotiations, paralysed since Netanyahu's right-wing government come to power after elections in May.
"I hope Mr Arafat and the president of Syria will come forward, will continue the negotiations and we will find a solution to all the problems," he said.
Mubarak said he thought a Hebron agreement was inevitable but also predicted catastrophe if the talks failed.
"There's nothing to be done but carry out what was agreed, otherwise it will be disaster -- everyone signing an agreement and then saying he wants to change it," he said.

Israel and the Palestinians signed an agreement on Hebron more than a year ago but Israel has been trying to change it on the grounds that the original did not provide enough security for the 400 Jewish settlers in the town.
The Egyptian president said he told Mordechai of his objections to Israel's policy of settling Jews in the West Bank.
"It is a very dangerous bomb that could put the peace process at stake. I gave him my opinion," he said.
